notes.text: Nevertheless — The calamity of this land and its inhabitants shall be great, yet not such as that which was brought upon it by the king of Assyria, who at first indeed dealt more gently with them, but afterwards rooted them out. He - God. Zebulun - These parts are particularly mentioned, because this storm fell most heavily upon them; but under them the other parts of the land are understood. Afterward - By Shalmaneser, who took Samaria, and carried Israel into captivity, 2 Kings xvii, 5, 6. Of which calamity, though yet to come, he speaks as if it were past, as the manner of the prophet is. The sea - In that part of the land which borders upon the sea, the lake Genesareth, upon which the portions of Zebulun and Naphtali bordered. Galilee - Or, Galilee of the Gentiles, namely, the upper Galilee, so called because it bordered upon the Gentiles.

The people — Israel and Judah. Darkness - The expression is general and so may well comprehend both calamity and ignorance, idolatry and profaneness, in which those parts were eminently involved. Have seen - Shall see at the coming of the Messiah.

Thou hast — Thou hast made good thy promise to Abraham concerning the multiplication of his seed, by gathering in the Gentiles to the Jews. Before thee - In thy presence, and in the place of thy worship.

The yoke — His burdensome yoke. The staff - The staff or staves by which he was forced to carry burdens upon his shoulders. The rod - Wherewith he beat him. Oppressor - Of all his oppressors, but especially of sin and the devil. As - When God destroyed the Midianites in so admirable a manner by three hundred men.

glossa.text:
*In the first time,* ((HIER.)) These two tribes were led into captivity by the Assyrians, etc., *as far as* it first saw the light of Christ preaching.

*The land of Zabulon.* ((ID.)) In which Christ first preached and wrought miracles: for there he turned water into wine, and chose the apostles.

*The way of the sea.* The sea in this place is the lake of Genezareth, which is made by the inflowing of the Jordan. Upon whose shore is Capharnaum, Tiberias, Bethsaida and Corozain, in which the Lord chiefly abode; and so: *The people that walked in darkness saw a great light.*

*Of the Galilee of the Gentiles.* There are two Galilees: one of the Gentiles, near to the Tyrians in the tribe of Nephtali; the other about Tiberias and the pool of Genesareth, in the tribe of Zabulon.

*In the region of the shadow of death.* ((ID.)) They are in the shadow of death who still live in sins: *in the region of the shadow of death,* they who have already gone down to the lower regions with dead works.

*Thou hast not magnified the joy.* To us, concerning the salvation of the Jews; for although they rejoice over the conversion of the Gentiles, yet they grieve over the rejection of the Jews.

 *They shall rejoice before thee,* etc. The prophet to Christ, concerning the disciples.

*For the yoke.* ((ID.)) Christ has a yoke, but a sweet one; the devil also, but one unbearable by its burden. And Christ has the princedom upon his shoulder, upon which he bore the cross; and the devil upon his shoulder a rod, wherewith he is proud.

*Of the exactor.* Of him, namely, that exacts. For daily he exacts from posterity, with usury, the coin of sin which he committed to the first man.

notes.text: Dwell. &c. — Have opportunity of constant attendance upon God. To behold - That there I may delight myself, in the contemplation of thy amiable and glorious majesty, and of thy infinite wisdom, holiness, justice, truth, and mercy.
The secret — In his tabernacle, into which mine enemies cannot come. He alludes to the ancient custom of offenders, who used to flee to the tabernacle or altar. Rock - A place high and inaccessible.
Away — From thy face or presence, or from the place of thy worship.

glossa.text:
*Unto the end.* ((AUG., CASS.)) First, David chosen, etc., *as far as* whence groaning and labouring in the sacrament; that he may rejoice in the reality.

 *The Lord is my light,* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the first anointing, through which the second is made sure, he speaks here.

*The Lord is the protector of my life.* ((AUG.)) He gives the life of the virtues, which he also protects, without which all his gifts are lost.

*Of whom shall I be afraid?* ((ID.)) Whom should the flesh fear, when it shall have put on corruption *corruptionem*; read *incorruptionem*, "incorruption".

*One thing I have asked.* ((AUG.)) This one house is eternal, in which one may abide always, where the days are eternal; why there? That I may contemplate the delight of God, which is the true good.

*All the days of my life.* ((AUG.)) That as long as I live, etc., *as far as* I will make manifest the work.

*That I may see.* ((ID.)) Another reading: *That I may contemplate the delight of the Lord,* that is, to this end, that at last he may appear, etc., *as far as* and therefore not rashly do I ask *one thing,* though a sinner.
*In secret*: ((AUG.)) as it were there are many parts, etc., *as far as* him whom presently he calls a rock.

*I have gone round.* ((AUG.)) Because he offered himself to me as a leader, etc., *as far as* that I might fulfil all his wills.

((HIER.)) Or I have looked round upon all created things, or the examples of the saints.

((AUG.)) I have gone round in mind all created things, etc., *as far as* the more ardently it desires.
*Hear, O Lord, my voice,* etc. ((CASS.)) What labour, what groaning? The prayer before the second anointing, that he may be able to have that which he also promises himself by the spirit of prophecy.
*To thee hath said.* ((CASS.)) *The heart,* the reason taught by thee, converses with thee of the one thing, that it may handle nothing other than what thou teachest.

*Turn not away.* ((AUG.)) Another asks here for temporal goods from God, and rejoices in what is given; this man asks nothing but *one thing.* Another, having them, fears him angered, lest he take them away; this man thinks there is no anger unless he *turn away his countenance,* even if he punish something in him; nothing more divine could he have said.

*Turn not aside.* ((AUG.)) He does not turn aside in anger, when he turns his face from sins; or, *turn not aside,* so as to let me slip in anger, that is, in what thou mayest punish; but that our weakness may be made more wary.

 *My saviour,* etc. ((AUG.)) As though: in vain hast thou created and re-created, etc., *as far as* he was chosen by the Lord through Samuel.

notes.text: Now I exhort you — Ye have faith and hope; secure love also. By the endearing name of our Lord Jesus Christ - lnfinitely preferable to all the human names in which ye glory. That ye all speak the same thing - They now spoke different things, ver. 12 And that there be no schisms among you - No alienation of affection from each other. Is this word ever taken in any other sense in scripture? But that ye be joined in the same mind - Affections, desires. And judgment - Touching all the grand truths of the gospel.

It hath been declared to me by them of the family of Chloe — Whom some suppose to have been the wife of Stephanas, and the mother of Fortunatus and Achaicus. By these three the Corinthians had sent their letter to St. Paul, chap. xvi, 17. That there are contentions - A word equivalent with schisms in the preceding verse.

Now this I say — That is, what I mean is this: there are various parties among you, who set themselves, one against an other, in behalf of the several teachers they admire. And I of Christ - They spoke well, if they had not on this pretense despised their teachers, chap. iv, 8 Perhaps they valued themselves on having heard Christ preach in his own person.

Is Christ divided — Are not all the members still under one head? Was not he alone crucified for you all; and were ye not all baptized in his name? The glory of Christ then is not to be divided between him and his servants; neither is the unity of the body to be torn asunder, seeing Christ is one still.
I thank God — (A pious phrase for the common one, "I rejoice,") that, in the course of his providence, I baptized none of you, but Crispus, once the ruler of the synagogue, and Caius.
Lest any should say that I had baptized in my own name — In order to attach them to myself.
I know not — That is, it does not at present occur to my memory, that I baptized any other.

For God did not send me to baptize — That was not my chief errand: those of inferior rank and abilities could do it: though all the apostles were sent to baptize also, Matt. xxviii, 19 But to preach the gospel - So the apostle slides into his general proposition: but not with wisdom of speech - With the artificial ornaments of discourse, invented by human wisdom. Lest the cross of Christ should be made of none effect - The whole effect of St. Paul's preaching was owing to the power of God accompanying the plain declaration of that great truth, "Christ bore our sins upon the cross." But this effect might have been imputed to another cause, had he come with that wisdom of speech which they admired.

To them that perish — By obstinately rejecting the only name whereby they can be saved. But to us who are saved - Now saved from our sins, and in the way to everlasting salvation, it is the great instrument of the power of God.

glossa.text: *I beseech.* Thus far he has praised the good. These being praised, he invites the others to the likeness of these.

*Of Chloe.* It is the name of a place or of a person. For to some it seems to be a place, as if it were said: from those who are at Antioch. But to others she seems to have been a woman devoted to God, with whom were many that worshipped God.

*Now this I say.* Here he begins to argue against the baptizers, in whom those men gloried. *I indeed.* Under his own name and that of the apostles he marks the false apostles, lest, if he were to say: in the name of this man or of that, he should seem to envy them, and to wish to claim it for himself. Or he set down the names of the good apostles, that he might show that if there is no glorying in the name of the greater, neither is there glorying in the name of those whose doctrine is depraved.

*Divided is* according to you *Christ,* as if he should say: You make many Christs, that is, many givers of graces. Or he who works the same thing in all is divided, while he is believed to work more in this man, less in that. Or because you say this, now Christ is divided from you, that is, separated: *Was Paul crucified?* By this truth which the Corinthians held, he makes them blush for the falsehoods: as by the resurrection of Christ, which they believed, he proves the resurrection of the dead, which they denied.

*I give thanks to God,* etc. ((AUG.)) Paul gives thanks to God that he baptized none of them, who, as though they had forgotten in whose name they had been baptized, were dividing themselves by the names of men. For since baptism given through a contemptible man avails as much as that given through an Apostle, so also it is known to be not his, but Christ's, etc.

*But to preach the gospel.* For even the less learned can baptize perfectly. But to preach the gospel perfectly is far more difficult and of rarer accomplishment. Therefore the teacher of the Gentiles, more excellent than many, says that he was sent to preach the gospel, not to baptize. Yet this he did at times, when necessity pressed. *Not in wisdom.* Against the wisdom of the world. *Not in wisdom of speech.* He means the wisdom of the philosophers, which is so called although it is not such: yet it is that which makes men wordy, through which the cross, that is, the death of Christ, is made void; and it is judged impossible according to nature that the immortal God should die. *Of speech.* The composition of words is sought there, where the truth itself does not commend itself with power for witness.

*To them that perish.* That is, to the wise men of the world, whose wisdom both perishes and is shown to be false, and who themselves are to be damned.

*The power of God.* In that, being slain, he conquered the devil and set man free, or he gives power to believers, by which miracles are done, when the matter requires.

notes.text: He retired into Galilee — This journey was not immediately after his temptation. He first went from Judea into Galilee, John i, 43; ii, 1. Then into Judea again, and celebrated the passover at Jerusalem, John ii, 13. He baptized in Judea while John was baptizing at Enon, John iii, 22, 23. All this time John was at liberty, John iii, 24. But the Pharisees being offended, John iv, 1; and John put in prison, he then took this journey into Galilee. Mark i, 14.
Leaving Nazareth — Namely, when they had wholly rejected his word, and even attempted to kill him, Luke iv, 29.
Galilee of the Gentiles — That part of Galilee which lay beyond Jordan was so called, because it was in a great measure inhabited by Gentiles, that is, heathens. Isaiah ix, 1, 2.
Here is a beautiful gradation, first, they walked, then they sat in darkness, and lastly, in the region of the shadow of death.

From that time Jesus began to preach — He had preached before, both to Jews and Samaritans, John iv, 41, 45. But from this time begin his solemn stated preaching. Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand - Although it is the peculiar business of Christ to establish the kingdom of heaven in the hearts of men, yet it is observable, he begins his preaching in the same words with John the Baptist: because the repentance which John taught still was, and ever will be, the necessary preparation for that inward kingdom. But that phrase is not only used with regard to individuals in whom it is to be established, but also with regard to the Christian Church, the whole body of believers. In the former sense it is opposed to repentance; in the latter the Mosaic dispensation.
Mark i, 16; Luke v, 1.
The Gospel of the kingdom — The Gospel, that is, the joyous message, is the proper name of our religion: as will be amply verified in all who earnestly and perseveringly embrace it.

glossa.text:
*And when he had heard. ((RAB.))* Here Matthew, like Mark and Luke, passes over the Lord's first coming into Galilee, after which, etc., *as far as, This beginning of miracles did Jesus.* And again: *John was not yet cast into prison.* 

*John,* etc. Which was for the Gospel's sake. Jesus, preaching this same thing more perfectly, gives place for a time and flees, that he may be an example to his own. *Into Galilee.* There are two Galilees: one is called the Galilee of the Jews, the other of the Gentiles, because of the dwelling of Gentiles there, which portion Solomon gave to the king of Tyre, who settled Gentiles there.

*Nazareth. ((RAB.))* From which Christ is called a Nazarene, is a village in Galilee beside mount Thabor, etc., *as far as* because in the midst of the Gentiles it stands firm for the spreading abroad of the word of God, that it may show to believers in peril the harbor of faith.

*The land of Zabulon. ((ID.))* The evangelist passes over what stands first; namely: *In the first time the land of Zabulon and the land of Nephtalim was lightened ((Isa. IX))*: as also what stands in the middle, etc., *as far as* but for a figure of those who are to be called from among the Gentiles, that which is of the Gentiles is here mentioned.

*The people. ((AUG.))* That people which was first led into captivity, and was in the darkness of vices, first saw the light of Christ's preaching. Thereafter the Gospel was scattered abroad among all. Whence it follows: *To them that dwell in the region.* 

*Of the shadow of death.* Death is in hell. The shadow of this death are sins, which are never without death. He therefore who wishes to flee death, let him avoid the shadow.

*From that time.* After he was baptized. Baptism makes men fit for preaching. *From that time,* that is, John having been delivered up: because when the law ceases the Gospel follows, as the sun follows the dawn. A humble master, who does not hinder the teaching of his disciple, but waits until he complete his course. In which he teaches that no one should despise a word from a lesser person. Whence the Apostle. *If anything be revealed to another, let the first hold his peace.* 

*Do penance.* The same things which the herald preaches: that it may be shown that he is no other than he who had cried in the voice. For Christ is the Word which cries in the Jordan by his instrument, and in all who from the beginning spoke anything by divine inspiration: and yet this man alone is the voice, because through him is shown the Word present, which the others announced from afar. For between the voice and the word there is nothing between, but as soon as the voice has sounded, straightway the word is perceived: as John, shut up, ceased: Christ shone forth in mighty works. Whence John is the figure of the prophets and of the law, who are truly the voice of the crying wisdom of God, of whom John is the end, and when they cease the Word alone, which had sounded in them, is shown by itself.

((RAB.)) This preaching of Christ, begun in Capharnaum with miracles flashing forth, is said, etc., *as far as* he began to preach when the Baptist was imprisoned.

*Who is called Peter.* Either when Andrew first brought him to him, this name was put upon him, when it is said: *Thou shalt be called Cephas ((Joan. I))*, which is interpreted *Peter:* although here he seems to promise it for the future. Or when he confessed: *Thou art Christ the Son of the living God,* it was said to him: *Thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church ((Matth. XVI))*.

((BEDA.)) Peter, *acknowledging:* Andrew, *manly:* which befits teachers: because these alone, etc., *as far as* but because the first man went out disobedient, the second entered in obedient ((RAB.)) Matthew says that he called the disciples after his dwelling at Capharnaum. John says, etc., *as far as* but before Jesus came into Cana of Galilee, Andrew brought Peter, yet they were not disciples.


*Casting a net.* Because those whom he sees often gaping after earthly gains he calls to heavenly desires, and through them, by the nets of the Gospel, he snatches others out of the deep of iniquity, whence he adds: *Come ye after me, and I will make you to be fishers of men [n: (Joan. I)]*.

*Fishers.* He who is about to fish goes through the places of fishing.

Mystically. When being incarnate he took flesh, he saw by his divinity in the sea of the world spiritual fishers: and to others he showed what they were, whom he had foreseen from eternity.

*Immediately.* Perfect obedience is to leave one's own things unfinished. Their nets being left: because even if afterwards they take them up again, it is not out of covetousness and the love of ownership. In these a pattern is given to those who wish to follow. The intention is changed, not the fishing, the nets are changed into doctrine, covetousness into the love of souls: the sea becomes the world, the ship the Church, the fishes good and evil men.

*He saw two others.* Behold, in these four the number of the evangelists is prefigured, who draw souls out of the world from the four quarters of the world.

They are called two and two, because charity is not save between two. A calling is spoken of: either according to the election of grace. Whence it is said: *Whom he called ((Rom. VIII))*, etc. Or according to that word: *Many are called ((Matth. X))*.

((AUG.)) It is asked how Matthew and Mark say that Jesus called them two by two: first Peter and Andrew, etc., *as far as* but he sent unlettered fishermen to preach for this reason, that faith might be reckoned to stand in the power of God, not in the eloquence of men.

*Of Zebedee, and John.* Zebedee, a fugitive, that is, the devil. James, a supplanter, who is helped by John, that is, by the grace of God. *And he called them. But they,* etc. He called others also, but it suffices to name these.

*And Jesus went about all Galilee.* His fellow workers being called, he presses on with preaching, teaching that a teacher ought to be untiring. *Teaching in the synagogues.* Teaching about morals, those subject to the active life. Preaching about things to come, those perfect in the contemplative life. Teaching the natural righteousnesses, namely chastity and humility and the like, which man has by nature. Preaching the Gospel of the kingdom. To the Gospel belongs the mystery of righteousness, a good beginning, the promise of beatitude, the remission of sins, adoption, resurrection, the heavenly inheritance, the fellowship of the angels.

*In the synagogues.* Nor let an idle teacher run about to no purpose, but let him preach where there are many.

*The Gospel.* Because righteousness is a trouble to one living in the flesh, the labor of righteousness is not undertaken unless the wage of the work be looked for. Therefore Christ preaches beatitude for good news, that he may stir men up to patience in good work.

*And healing.* To cure sickness and infirmity was no great thing, since they were to die afterwards. But it was done for this reason, that they might so be raised up to the kingdom. Morally instructing preachers to minister earthly supports also to their subjects, and so to draw them to the kingdom.

echoes.text: Take wise men of understanding and well known according to your tribes, and I will make them heads over you.”
echoes.note: Paul's plea that they be 'perfected together in the same mind and the same judgment,' against 'contentions,' faintly recalls Moses' appointment of wise leaders to adjudicate strife among a quarreling people. The thematic coherence (concord versus faction) is reasonable, but verbal contact is slight and the appeal to unity is a general topos.

echoes.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!
echoes.note: 'How good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity' supplies a scriptural ideal of fraternal concord behind Paul's exhortation that 'brothers' avoid divisions. The resonance is thematic and the term 'brothers' is shared, but the volume is faint and the motif diffuse.

echoes.text: therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous work among this people, even a marvelous work and a wonder; and the wisdom of their wise men will perish, and the understanding of their prudent men will be hidden.”
echoes.note: Verse 19 quotes with formula ('it is written') Isaiah 29:14 LXX: 'I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will thwart/bring to nothing.' Volume is maximal (verbatim citation), and the thematic coherence is exact: God's overturning of human sagacity is the engine of Paul's whole cross-versus-wisdom argument.

echoes.text: The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, “I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?” Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now; and let them know what Yahweh of Armies has purposed concerning Egypt.
echoes.note: 'Where is the wise?' (v.20) recalls the taunt against Egypt's counselors: 'Where then are your wise men?... let them tell.' The interrogative form mocking discredited sages is distinctive, and recurrence within Isaiah's wisdom-polemic strengthens coherence with Paul's rhetorical questions about the wise of this age.

echoes.text: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?
echoes.note: 'Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighed?' supplies the closest LXX template for Paul's triad 'Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater?' The naming of the 'scribe (grammateus)' is the load-bearing verbal link, and the context of a vanished officialdom after divine deliverance coheres with Paul's point.

echoes.text: He leads counselors away stripped. He makes judges fools.
echoes.note: Job's hymn declares that God 'leads counselors away stripped and makes fools of judges,' overturning the wisdom of the prudent (cf. Job 12:20, 'he takes away the discernment of the elders'). The thematic coherence with God 'making foolish the wisdom of this world' is strong, and the recurrence of the divine reversal-of-sages motif supports a real echo.

echoes.text: who frustrates the signs of the liars, and makes diviners mad; who turns wise men backward, and makes their knowledge foolish;
echoes.note: 'Frustrating the signs of liars and making fools of diviners, turning wise men back and making their knowledge foolish'—this Deutero-Isaiah oracle nearly paraphrases v.20's 'Hasn't God made foolish the wisdom of this world?' The verbal cluster (wise/foolish/knowledge) is dense and the polemic against pretended wisdom coheres tightly.

echoes.text: He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel, he will be a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
echoes.note: 'A stumbling block to Jews' (v.23) draws on Isaiah's image of the LORD as 'a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense' to the houses of Israel. Volume is good on the distinctive 'stumbling/offense' lexeme, recurrence is strong in Paul (Rom 9:33), and the irony of God's saving act becoming an obstacle to Israel coheres precisely.

echoes.text: The wise men are disappointed. They are dismayed and trapped. Behold, they have rejected Yahweh’s word. What kind of wisdom is in them?
echoes.note: 'The wise men shall be put to shame... they have rejected the word of the LORD, and what wisdom is in them?' parallels Paul's claim that the world's wisdom failed to know God. The shaming of the wise and the linkage of wisdom to receiving God's word cohere, though the verbal contact is moderate.

echoes.text: Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh, “Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious cornerstone of a sure foundation. He who believes shall not act hastily.
echoes.note: The 'tested stone' laid in Zion, paired in Pauline usage with Isaiah 8:14, underlies the 'stumbling block' of v.23 and the foundation-stone motif of the proclaimed Christ. The connection is figural and mediated through Paul's wider stone testimonia rather than directly verbal here.

echoes.text: “Look among the nations, watch, and wonder marvelously; for I am working a work in your days, which you will not believe though it is told you.
echoes.note: 'I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if told' offers a scriptural template for God accomplishing salvation through means the wise reject as incredible. The thematic coherence with the cross as God's unbelievable 'good pleasure' is suggestive, but the verbal link is faint.
echoes.lxxText: Behold, ye despisers, and look, and wonder marvelously, and vanish: for I work a work in your days, which ye will in no wise believe, though a man declare it to you.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations. The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: vv.15-16 quote Isa 9:1-2 with formula 'that it might be fulfilled... through Isaiah': 'land of Zebulun and Naphtali... Galilee of the Gentiles, the people who sat in darkness saw a great light.' High Volume formula citation; Matthew geographically anchors Jesus' Galilean ministry in Isaiah's promise of light to the despised northern tribes first to suffer Assyrian conquest.

echoes.text: and look to the earth, and see distress, darkness, and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick darkness.
echoes.note: The immediately preceding context of the quotation — 'gloom of anguish... region and shadow of death' — supplies the contrast of darkness the 'great light' dispels; Matthew's citation spans the Isa 8/9 seam.

echoes.text: In the days of those kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed, nor shall its sovereignty be left to another people; but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.
echoes.note: 'The God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed' grounds 'the Kingdom of Heaven' (v.17); Matthew's signature 'Kingdom of Heaven' reflects Danielic heaven-kingdom expectation. Thematic, recurrent.

echoes.text: In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel Beth Maacah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carried them captive to Assyria.
echoes.note: Tiglath-pileser's deportation of Zebulun/Naphtali (Galilee) sets the historical 'darkness' Isa 9 reverses; the named tribes carry this exile memory. Background, faint.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come... nations shall come to your light' — recurrent Isaianic light-to-the-nations theme reinforcing 'Galilee of the Gentiles' seeing the light. Thematic, contested as a distinct source.

echoes.text: “I, Yahweh, have called you in righteousness, and will hold your hand, and will keep you, and make you a covenant for the people, as a light for the nations; to open the blind eyes, to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
echoes.note: The servant given 'as a light to the nations, to open eyes that are blind' resonates with Jesus as the light dawning on Gentile Galilee. Faint thematic recurrence.

echoes.text: “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach against it, for their wickedness has come up before me.” But Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh. He went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish; so he paid its fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand' (v.17) opens with the prophetic call to repentance characteristic of Jonah/the prophets; Matthew later pairs Jonah-Nineveh with repentance preaching (12:41). Faint, generic prophetic echo.

echoes.text: Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ways, says the Lord Yahweh. Return, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin. Cast away from you all your transgressions, in which you have transgressed; and make yourself a new heart and a new spirit: for why will you die, house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of him who dies, says the Lord Yahweh: therefore turn yourselves, […]
echoes.note: 'Repent and turn... why will you die?' — the prophetic summons to repentance underlies Jesus' inaugural proclamation. Generic, contested.

echoes.text: So he departed there, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing, with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed over to him, and cast his mantle on him. He left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said, “Let me please kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.” He said to him, “Go back again; for what have I done to you?” He returned from following him, and took the yoke of oxen, and killed them, […]
echoes.note: Elijah's call of Elisha — who is plowing, leaves his oxen, and immediately follows — patterns the immediate abandonment of nets/boat/father by the fishermen (vv.20, 22). Strong narrative parallel of prophetic call met by instant, total following.

echoes.text: Behold, I will send for many fishermen, says Yahweh, and they shall fish them up; and afterward I will send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the clefts of the rocks.
echoes.note: 'I will send for many fishers, says the LORD, and they shall fish them' — the prophetic 'fishers' image stands behind 'I will make you fishers for men' (v.19). Verbal borrowing of the fishing-for-people metaphor, though Jeremiah's is judgment and Jesus' is gathering.

echoes.text: It shall happen, that every living creature which swarms, in every place where the rivers come, shall live; and there shall be a very great multitude of fish; for these waters have come there, and the waters of the sea shall be healed, and everything shall live wherever the river comes. It shall happen, that fishermen shall stand by it: from En Gedi even to En Eglaim shall be a place for the spreading of nets; their fish shall be after their kinds, as the […]
echoes.note: Fishermen spreading nets at the life-giving river/sea of the eschatological temple vision; faint resonance with calling fishermen into kingdom-mission abundance.

echoes.text: The Lord Yahweh has sworn by his holiness that behold, “The days shall come on you that they will take you away with hooks, and the last of you with fish hooks.
echoes.note: 'He will take you away with hooks, the last of you with fishhooks' — another prophetic fishing-as-gathering image contributing to the recurrent metaphor behind 'fishers for men.' Faint, judgment-toned.

echoes.text: and make men like the fish of the sea, like the creeping things, that have no ruler over them? He takes up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his net, and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
echoes.note: Humanity caught 'like fish of the sea... they bring them up with a net' — recurrent OT trope of people-as-fish-in-nets resonant with the fishing-for-men commission. Contested.

echoes.text: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped. Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
echoes.note: Jesus 'healing every disease and every sickness' (v.23-24) enacts the Isaianic restoration where 'the eyes of the blind shall be opened... the lame leap'; Matthew elsewhere makes this explicit (11:5). Thematic Coherence with the in-breaking kingdom.

echoes.text: Surely he has borne our sickness, and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.
echoes.note: 'He bore our sicknesses' — the healing summary anticipates Matthew's own citation of Isa 53:4 over the healings in 8:17, making this servant-healing theology a likely background here too.

echoes.text: who forgives all your sins; who heals all your diseases;
echoes.note: 'Who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases' — the divine prerogative to heal 'all diseases' is exercised by Jesus, a faint resonance of God's healing kingship.

echoes.text: But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out, and leap like calves of the stall.
echoes.note: 'The sun of righteousness shall rise with healing in its wings' — eschatological dawning healing connects to the 'light dawned' (v.16) now realized in the healing ministry. Faint, thematic.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
By the sea he called them: Follow me.
And they left their nets at once.
The kingdom of heaven has come near.
We turn, and we follow.
Come, let us worship the Light who calls us.
We will follow. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Dawn comes up grey over the lake, and into a land that has sat a long time in the dark, a great light is breaking.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
A man walks the shoreline and stops where the fishermen are working, and he says two words that change a life: follow me.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
And they do — nets still wet in their hands, the boat left rocking, the old life dropped on the sand.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
Whom shall we fear, then, with that light on the water and that voice calling our name?
The Lord is my light and my salvation. Thanks be to God!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A great light dawns on the people in the dark.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
He calls along the shore: come, follow me.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
They leave the nets behind and follow him.
The Lord is my light and my salvation.
Come, let us worship the Light who calls.
The Lord is my light and my salvation. Thanks be to God!
